questions.q: When does branch-per-experiment tend to fit a research team better than trunk-based development with config flags?
options: When the experiment only varies a hyperparameter already exposed in the config
When the experiment requires actually changing the model architecture or training loop, not just a config value
Branch-per-experiment is always strictly better regardless of the change
When the team has fewer than two researchers
questions.explain: Branch-per-experiment isolates changes that touch code structure, such as the model or training loop. Config-only variation is better handled through trunk-based development with Hydra overrides, since it avoids the overhead of long-lived branches.

questions.q: What command retrieves the current commit hash so it can be logged alongside an experiment-tracking run?
options: git status
git rev-parse HEAD
git log --all
git branch -a
questions.explain: git rev-parse HEAD returns the full hash of the current commit, which can be captured in a script (e.g. via subprocess.check_output) and logged as a field in a tool like W&B or MLflow.

questions.q: Why is logging a commit hash alongside a run's results worthless if the working tree had uncommitted changes at launch time?
options: Because git cannot compute a hash with uncommitted changes present
Because the logged hash points to the last committed code, not the actual code (including uncommitted edits) that ran
Because uncommitted changes automatically get deleted before a run starts
Because wandb.init() refuses to run with a dirty working tree
questions.explain: The commit hash only describes the last committed state. If the working tree has uncommitted edits when the run launches, the actual code that ran differs from what the hash represents, breaking provenance unless guarded against.

questions.q: To fully answer 'what produced this number,' what two pieces of information need to be logged together for a given run?
options: The researcher's name and the date
The exact commit hash (the code) and the resolved config snapshot (the configuration)
The GPU model and the cloud region
The total runtime and the final loss value
questions.explain: The commit hash identifies exactly what code ran, and Hydra's per-run resolved config snapshot identifies exactly what configuration it ran with. Both together, not either alone, make a result's provenance fully recoverable.

questions.q: What is one lightweight habit suggested for making headline results easy to trace back to exact code months later?
options: Deleting old branches as soon as a paper is published
Tagging the specific commit behind a headline result, e.g. git tag paper-table2-row3
Avoiding git entirely in favor of manual file backups
Renaming the main branch after every experiment
questions.explain: Tagging a commit that corresponds to a specific reported result (like a paper's table row) creates a durable, easy-to-find reference point, which pays off when someone later asks to see the exact code behind that number.
